contracts.rationale: asynchronous reset clears the valid flag in the same cycle
asynchronous reset clears the accumulator in the same cycle
valid_out is a one-cycle pulse: the counter restarts as soon as it fires
after a pulse the design needs valid_in to make progress (ready_add = !valid_out | valid_in)
the sample accepted right after a pulse starts a new accumulation, so the total is one sample wide
four 8-bit samples cannot exceed the width of the output register

out_of_grammar.why_not_minable: a disjunctive consequent is not produced by any template; the earlier version of ACC7 needed it because a reset inside the window discharges the obligation. If the nominal traces keep resets outside the window this is unnecessary

a bounded-response guarantee whose window can lose the assumption. The invariants rst_n == 1 and valid_in == 1 hold at the sample the guarantee fires on, but the environment may drop either one inside the five-cycle window, and the accumulator then stalls. Constraining the whole window needs a temporal assumption, which is not an invariant
same as ACC7, without the valid_out == 0 precondition

assumptions.why: the environment keeps offering samples. The design only advances its counter while valid_out is low, so a sample offered and then withdrawn stalls the accumulation: the bounded-response guarantees are owed only under a continuous stream
